evidence.summary: Plan 4 is a measurement, not a fix: 10 headless runs (5 widgets x Claude Code and Codex) on the packed SDK, imported into the desktop app; the result is one report. Decisions: controller launches agents; all 10 runs; keep clock and counter on the main screen, other three are checks; no fixes or reruns after a failed run (decision 4); default models; clean profiles; no browser for agents (decision 9). Success: widget created and imports on the first attempt. Failure: agent reads dashboard sources outside the allowed list, check/build fails, no import, or pass criteria not met. Non-goals: fixing docs/types/skill/SDK, npm publishing, Windows and Linux, agents other than Claude Code and Codex, code quality beyond pass criteria. Status line: approved (changed 2026-10-22, commit c6cda69).

Plan for the spec above: run root outside the repository; tooling (echo server, runner, read audit); clean Claude Code and Codex profiles; the five run sentences; setup, runs, import through the Orca browser on http://127.0.0.1:3101; one committed report (Task 7). Its Codex profile step copies only the auth file. Plan has no results section.

Round 1 verdict: fail. 3 of 10 runs pass every criterion (claude-4, codex-2 under a contaminated profile, codex-5). Five runs read compiled SDK files (claude-1, claude-2, claude-3, claude-5, codex-1). codex-1 renders blank; codex-4 does not fit its 4x4 default size; codex-3 produced nothing (infrastructure fault, contaminated Codex profile). Every deliverable passed check and build and imported on the first attempt. Infrastructure faults: contaminated Codex profile, shared /tmp leftovers, Claude run on the user's account and real HOME at the user's request.

Round 2 on branch fix/widget-sdk-acceptance-gaps: verdict fail. 8 of 10 runs pass every criterion; 0 forbidden reads; 0 questions. codex-1 fails (clock clipped when wider than tall); codex-4 fails (JPY hidden and error line overlaps rates at 4x4). Round-1 gaps closed by SDK and docs changes (373f0fb, 02d5ea5). A false 8 px dev-shell overflow before mount was found and fixed after the run (f781bc4). Follow-up reruns: codex-1 pass after 699b073; codex-4 fail at 4x4 in sandboxed Codex, pass at 4x4 without the sandbox (e9760b0 advice). Chrome cannot start inside the Codex macOS workspace-write sandbox. HTTP checks waited about 6 hours on a bundled-node network outage (infrastructure, cause inferred). Not checked: the desktop app's own WKWebView window; npm create with published packages (packages were tarballs).

Round 5, full rerun of all 10 runs on main at f7ddb99 (SDK and create-widget tarballs and desktop app rebuilt from that commit). Verdict: pass on the acceptance criteria; 10 of 10 runs pass every criterion. Every deliverable passed check and build, matched the control build and imported on the first attempt. Every agent kept its title; 0 forbidden reads. Each agent took screenshots of its widget with the documented recipe. claude-4 took 40.3 minutes; no run hit the 45-minute cap. Open findings: headless screenshot recipe unreliable; false dev-shell overflow before first measure; macOS Keychain dialog from headless Chrome; no message when auto-placement finds no free space. Rulings: Codex ran without its sandbox; fresh Codex profile with auth.json and config.toml. The report lists no infrastructure faults.

scope.text: Acceptance run of the widget SDK: 10 headless agent sessions (clock, counter, decorative, HTTP and secret widgets, each in Claude Code and Codex) against tarballs of @lifedashboard/widget-sdk and @lifedashboard/create-widget, then imported into the desktop app and checked in the Orca browser.

Final full rerun (round 5, main at f7ddb99): 10 of 10 runs pass every acceptance criterion; every deliverable passed check and build, matched the control build and imported on the first attempt; every agent kept its title; 0 forbidden reads.

Earlier rounds, superseded by round 5: round 1 (report f94471d) had 3 of 10 passing runs, 5 runs that read compiled SDK files, codex-1 blank and codex-4 clipped. Round 2 (report 8f66234, Codex results f7ddb99) had 8 of 10 passing, codex-1 clipped when wider than tall and codex-4 overlapping at 4x4.
SDK and docs changes made between rounds to close the gaps the reports recorded: 373f0fb, 02d5ea5, f781bc4, 93da11a, 699b073, e9760b0.

Committed reports: docs/superpowers/reports/2026-10-20-widget-sdk-acceptance-report.md, docs/superpowers/reports/2026-10-21-widget-sdk-acceptance-round2-report.md and docs/superpowers/reports/2026-10-21-widget-sdk-acceptance-round5-report.md. Raw logs, generated projects and screenshots stay outside the repository in /Volumes/ExtendSSD/ld-acceptance-2026-10-20 and are not archived.

followUps.text: Headless screenshot recipe is unreliable: blank or loading frames, parallel Chrome hangs, claude-4 spent most of 40 minutes on them. Proposed fix: ld-widget shot. Commit 2c118a4 adds it after the round 5 report; no recorded run exercises it.

False dev-shell overflow record before the first measure (round 5 finding). Commit bbf3f7f, subject 'skip the overflow probe until the frame has a size', comes after the round 5 report; no recorded run covers it.
Headless Chrome raises a macOS Keychain dialog under a test HOME. Proposed --use-mock-keychain in the recipe; not recorded as applied.
No message reaches the user when auto-placement finds no free space at a widget's default size; the widget was not placed and the report did not investigate further.

risks.text: Round 5 Codex runs were unsandboxed, so their results may overstate the default sandboxed Codex setup. The report records this as a ruling.
Each widget and agent pair ran once per round, so each round 5 pass is a single run.
Agents obtained a headless browser despite decision 9 (Playwright from caches or /tmp, or system Chrome). The reports record these attempts as findings.

Infrastructure faults in rounds 1 and 2: a contaminated Codex profile stopped codex-3 in round 1; codex-1 reused leftovers in /tmp; a bundled-node network outage in round 2 held HTTP checks for about 6 hours (cause inferred). The round 5 report lists no infrastructure fault.
The desktop app's own WKWebView window was not checked; all checks ran in the Orca browser on the app origin.

decisions.text: Plan 4 measures and reports; it does not fix. Fixes are a later plan that the user decides on after reading the report. Rationale: user decision, recorded in the spec's Intent.

Success: the widget is created and imports into the main dashboard on the first attempt. Failure: the agent reads dashboard sources outside the allowed list (the generated project's own files, node_modules/@lifedashboard/*/docs/, and .d.ts files), check or build fails, the folder does not import, or the widget fails the pass criteria. Rationale: user's words in the spec.
Agents get no browser, as a new user's terminal agent has none; an agent may not install one. Rationale: the setup must match a new user. Any attempt is recorded as a finding.
On a failed run the controller does not fix or rerun; it completes all 10 runs and writes one report. Rationale: user decision (decision 4). Later rounds departed from this; see deviations.

Clean profiles: no user-level CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, plugins, skills, hooks or MCP servers, so each run matches a new user. Codex uses a fresh CODEX_HOME with the auth file only, because --ignore-user-config alone does not stop the user's global AGENTS.md in ~/.codex from loading. Rationale: spec Constraints.

Clock and counter from both agents stay on the main screen as the kept widgets; decorative, HTTP and secret are checks and are removed after the report. Rationale: the user chose free space on the main screen because the board has no screen management.

Pass criteria: the clock is frameless on first placement (builtin:bare, no card frame), follows the theme, shows the local time and moves; the counter changes value, keeps it across an app reload, and changes its title from settings; decorative animates and fills its rectangle at every size; HTTP shows data, refreshes and shows a readable failure; secret shows UNAVAILABLE before entry and [REDACTED] after.
